comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Plan review on this ticket took three rounds, and every finding was correct. Recording them
because two would have been silent failures, not loud ones.

ROUND 1, finding A (G1G2): I put the "re-probe the lock between tickets" work in
`compact_trigger.py`. The per-ticket loop is not there — it is `compact_all_cli`'s loop in
`compact.py:386`. `run_sweep` only probes once before calling it. Wrong file for the fix.

ROUND 1, finding B (G6): THE IMPORTANT ONE. I named
`authorship.build_introducing_commit_map` as the one-pass replacement. That builder is keyed by
event PATH, but `_build_authorship_ledger` looks up `position_commits.get(position_str)`
(`compact_txn.py:127`) — by POSITION. A path-keyed map misses EVERY lookup, so every event
falls through to the per-event `resolve_event_commit`, silently re-introducing the exact
per-event walks this ticket exists to remove. The output would have been correct and the
performance unchanged, with nothing to notice. The right primitive is the position-keyed
sibling `build_position_commit_map` (`attest/authorship.py:466`), which I verified reads
position keys, walks history once, and falls back per-entry fail-closed.

That finding also changed a test: my "one walk per sweep" criterion counted the per-sweep
BUILDER only, which a key mismatch would still satisfy. It now counts the per-event resolvers
too, so a silent fallback fails the test instead of passing on identical output. A ledger-parity
test alone could never have caught this.

ROUND 2 (G1G2): `_build_authorship_ledger` has a second consumer I had not enumerated —
`compact_rebuild.py:160`, the fsck SNAPSHOT-rebuild path — plus six existing test call sites
passing `(paths, None)` positionally. Confirmed by grep rather than taken on faith. So the new
map parameter is OPTIONAL (keyword, default None): the rebuild path folds ONE ticket, where a
per-ticket walk is already the right cost, and it stays untouched. Added an acceptance criterion
that calling without the argument yields the same ledger.

The pattern across all three: I was reaching for a plausible-looking primitive and a plausible
scope without checking the key shape or the consumer set. The reviewer checked both. Worth
noting that the two findings a passing test suite would NOT have caught are exactly the two I
would have shipped.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Pushed: change 1739 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1739 (commit b8345508c9,
on merged main 2af5a4c773).

Local verification:
- integration tier: 194 passed, 1 skipped.
- ruff, mypy (527 files), module-size contract, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0.
- main tier: 12846 passed, 52 skipped, 3 FAILED.

The three main-tier failures all pass in ISOLATION (10/10 when re-run together, no parallelism),
and two are in code this change does not touch:
- `test_plan_review_gate.py::test_dependency_file_deletion_invalidates`
- `test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py::test_in_flight_refusal_clears_owned_pause_before_mutation[fsck]`
The third is one of MINE — `test_no_history_walk_runs_while_the_store_lock_is_held` — and it
failed in SETUP, not on its assertion: "rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit f…".
That is the store-contention signature, not a claim about lock-held walks.

I am not calling those flaky on one data point. A second full main-tier run is going now, and
this machine is under genuine load (the live full-store compaction stall is still running on the
real tracker — the same one that made an earlier `rebar comment` here wait 429s), which is
exactly the condition that produces git-contention failures in temp stores. CI is the
authoritative check and runs on clean runners; if it reproduces any of the three I will treat
them as real and stop.

What 1739 fixes: the sweep built one `git log --full-history` walk PER TICKET inside the store
write lock. It now builds ONE position-keyed map for the whole run before taking any lock, so
the critical section holds only the SNAPSHOT write, the renames and the commit. Plus scoped
staging (no more `git add -A` sweeping a concurrent writer's in-flight event into the compaction
commit) and a mid-run re-yield so a sweep that began on a quiet store stands aside when writers
arrive.

RED verified: reverting just the map threading and the scoped add fails three of the seven new
tests, including "no history walk runs while the store lock is held".

Two gates caught me while implementing, both correctly:
- the complexity ratchet flagged `compact_all_cli` as NEW debt (17 > 15). I extracted
  `_run_sweep`, `_sweep_position_map`, `_sweep_should_yield` and `_sweep_one_ticket` rather than
  raise the ceiling.
- my first "bystander" test was hollow: the innocent ticket was itself a fold candidate, so
  staging its directory was CORRECT and the test proved nothing. Rebuilt it as a settled,
  already-folded ticket — the faithful shape of a quiet ticket another session is appending to.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
1739 advisories fixed, and the second one exposed that THREE of my assertions were vacuous.

Advisory 1 (maintainability): the re-yield log counted `compacted + skipped`, omitting errored
tickets, so "yielding after N ticket(s)" understated what the sweep had processed. One-line fix.

Advisory 2 (tests): `test_the_map_argument_is_optional_for_the_rebuild_path` asserted only
`isinstance(ledger, list)` — which `_build_authorship_ledger` returns for essentially any input,
including a broken None-default branch producing empty or wrong values. Correct: a test that
cannot fail is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage.

Strengthening it to assert CONTENT immediately failed — the ledger was EMPTY. That exposed a
fixture defect underneath, which had also silently hollowed out two more assertions:

`_build_authorship_ledger` SKIPS any event without an `author_sig`, and my fixture created
unsigned events. So:
- the parity test was comparing `[] == []`;
- the "no per-event fallback" half of the walk-count test held trivially, because with no
  signed events the map is never consulted at all.

Fixed by giving the fixture real signed events AND COMMITTING them. Both halves matter: the
position map is built from `git log`, so an uncommitted event cannot be in it and the ledger
would fall back to the per-event resolver — the fixture would have proven the opposite of its
claim. The signature is synthetic, which is fine and documented: `identify_signer` records a
null `signer_pubkey` for a foreign signature and the entry is still recorded.

The strengthened test then caught one more error of mine: I asserted a top-level `commit_sha`,
but it is nested under `position`. Real entries look like
`{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position: {commit_sha, position}}`.

AND a near-miss worth recording. My first RED check for the walk-count test reported PASS with
the fix reverted — which would have meant the test had no power. The revert had silently not
applied: my string replacement no longer matched after `ruff format` reflowed the call. I only
caught it by counting the replacements instead of trusting the edit. Re-run with a verified
revert (2 occurrences removed), both walk tests fail as they should. I had been one step from
recording "RED verified" on a no-op.

Gates after all of it: ruff, mypy 527 files, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0, 7/7 sweep
tests. Re-pushed 1739 (LLM-Review +1 reset by the new patch set, as expected).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Flake hypothesis CONFIRMED, and I repeated a process mistake I had already recorded.

The second main-tier run came back 12849 passed, 52 skipped, 3 errors. None of the three
ORIGINAL failures reproduced:
- `test_no_history_walk_runs_while_the_store_lock_is_held` (mine, had failed in SETUP with a git
  commit error) — passed;
- `test_plan_review_gate.py::test_dependency_file_deletion_invalidates` — passed;
- `test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py::...[fsck]` — passed.

So all three were contention flakes under parallel load on a machine also running the live
full-store compaction stall, exactly as triaged. Two data points now, plus all ten passing in
isolation.

The 3 errors in THIS run were entirely my own: "Test moved the repo HEAD
(b8345508c9 -> 61936faa00): it committed i…" — I amended the commit while the tier was still
running, so the repo-commit guard fired on tests that assert HEAD stability. That is the SECOND
time this session I have done it; I wrote "Lesson recorded for myself: do not amend while a
suite is in flight" on the barbet ticket earlier and then did it again about ten hours later.
Recording it here rather than quietly re-running, because a lesson I write down and then repeat
is worth more as a visible pattern than as a note.

A clean tier is now running on the amended commit 61936faa00 with nothing else touching the
repo.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INDEPENDENT FIELD EVIDENCE from a different lane (the rich-text epic `vigilant-erasable-pony`). I hit this from the outside and filed `unfair-jocund-giraffe` before finding this ticket; that one is being closed as a duplicate and its observations are carried here so nothing is lost with it.

## Measured impact on an unrelated session
Two separate sweeps blocked this session's work today:
- One held `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` for **24+ minutes**, sitting at **0.0% CPU** the whole time (I/O-bound on git, not spinning). It aborted a `rebar set-file-impact` and then a `rebar transition ... closed` — the latter AFTER its completion verification had already run, so the LLM work was paid for and discarded.
- A second was spawned by a DIFFERENT worktree's close (`ci-config-schema-gate`) and blocked me again minutes later. So the blast radius is host-wide across worktrees, not per-checkout.

Observed command, confirming the per-ticket walk this ticket names:
```
git -c log.showSignature=false -C <tracker> log --diff-filter=A --full-history \
    --no-renames --format=%H -- '*<event-id>*.json'
```
Note the LEADING-WILDCARD pathspec, which defeats any pathspec fast path, so each walk is a full-history scan.

## Two things a fix should probably cover, in case they are not already in 1739's scope
1. **The failure is unreadable from the outside.** What a blocked session sees is `flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: pid=... held=47s)` — a pid with no indication that the holder is optional housekeeping. I only identified it via `lsof`/`ps`. If the sweep announced itself in the lock holder record (or the lock error named it), an operator would know immediately that SIGTERMing it is safe rather than treating it as a mystery hang.
2. **Nothing tells an operator that killing it is safe.** `run_sweep`'s own docstring guarantees "a skipped sweep is a no-op for correctness (the events stay live and the next trigger folds them)", which is exactly the licence needed — but that guarantee lives in a source docstring, not anywhere a blocked user would look. I relied on reading the source before killing it, twice.

## What I did operationally, for the record
SIGTERMed the sweeps rather than waiting them out, on the strength of that documented no-op guarantee. Both releases were clean and no store inconsistency followed. Recording it so the behaviour is a data point for 1739 rather than an unexplained intervention in the store history.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
1739 patch set 2 advisories: one was a CORRECTNESS REGRESSION I introduced, and it is worse
than the reviewer stated.

## The empty-map path made things worse than before the change

`_sweep_position_map` returned `{}` when the map could not be built (git failure), and
`_run_sweep` threaded that into every fold. But
`compact_txn._build_authorship_ledger` rebuilds its own per-ticket map only when the argument
`is None` (`compact_txn.py:114`). An empty dict is a perfectly valid map that simply misses
every lookup — so every event fell through to `resolve_event_commit`, then
`resolve_position_commit`, PER EVENT, INSIDE the store write lock.

That is not "degrading to the old behaviour". It is the full bug-7084 pathology — per-EVENT
full-history walks under the lock, the 6.78s-per-event case — strictly worse than the
per-ticket walk this whole ticket exists to remove. And my own comment on that line asserted
the opposite: "an empty map simply restores the per-ticket behaviour". It restores the per-event
behaviour.

Fixed: `_sweep_position_map` now returns `dict | None` and yields `None` on failure AND on an
empty result, so each fold rebuilds its own per-ticket map — the honest degradation. Added a
test that injects a builder failure and asserts the fallback is per-TICKET (>=1 ticket_map
build) and NOT per-event (0 per_event, 0 per_position). Verified RED against the `{}` version
with a counted revert (1 -> 1) rather than a trusted string edit.

## The second advisory was another half-assertion of mine

`test_the_sweep_commit_does_not_steal_a_concurrent_writers_event` asserted only that the stray
file was ABSENT from the commit — never that the legitimately folded SNAPSHOT was PRESENT. So
it would have passed if my scoped `git add -- {tid}/` staged nothing at all, "fixing" the theft
by committing nothing. Added the positive half.

## Also caught by the gates, not by me

`mypy` rejected the change: I updated `_sweep_position_map`'s return type but my edit to
`_sweep_one_ticket`'s parameter annotation silently did not apply — the target string had been
reflowed by `ruff format`. Same stale-string trap as the RED-check near-miss earlier today, and
the second time in one session that an edit I believed had applied had not. I am now verifying
replacement counts rather than trusting `str.replace`, and the typechecker caught what I did
not.

Gates green after all of it: ruff, mypy 527 files, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0, 39
tests across the three compaction suites. Amended and pushed BEFORE starting the tiers this
time, so nothing races them.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
BOOKKEEPING STATUS: already durable — no re-post needed. The retry landed while I was reading
the other lane's comment. Verified programmatically: 6 comments, with the reviewer's
`{}`-vs-`None` catch and the half-assertion catch both present. I am not duplicating them.

## The kill — final corroborating data point

A live PRE-FIX sweep had to be MANUALLY TERMINATED to unblock the fleet: pid 98440,
`compact_trigger.run_sweep` from the `pony2-richtext` worktree, 26 minutes elapsed, killed
mid-hold at 201s into a single lock acquisition. Three agents' store writes were blocked behind
it. `rebar doctor` shows all locks free afterwards.

I experienced this from inside: my own `rebar comment` on this ticket exhausted 11 retry passes
against a holder reported at 867s, and a later attempt produced no output at all. I could not
reliably write to the ticket store while documenting the fix for why the ticket store cannot be
written to.

That makes the evidence chain for this ticket complete and independent at three points:
1. operator profiling (fresh `git log --full-history` child every few seconds at ~100% CPU);
2. a different lane's session (`vigilant-erasable-pony`) blocked twice, once for 24+ minutes at
   0.0% CPU — I/O-bound on git, not spinning — losing a `transition ... closed` AFTER its
   completion verification had already been paid for;
3. this manual kill, plus my own 867s write starvation.

## What the other lane's observation adds, and it sharpens the diagnosis

The command they captured is:
```
git ... log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames --format=%H -- '*<event-id>*.json'
```
That LEADING-WILDCARD, per-EVENT pathspec is `resolve_event_commit`'s
(`attest/authorship.py:139` globs `<position>-*.json`), NOT
`build_ticket_position_commit_map`'s directory prefix. So the deployed sweep is not merely
doing one walk per ticket — it is falling through to PER-EVENT walks for every position its
per-ticket map misses, and a leading wildcard defeats pathspec pruning so each one is a full
history scan. The real deployed cost is worse than the ticket description states.

1739 covers exactly this: the whole-store position map is built once, and the test asserts
`per_event == 0` and `per_position == 0` — i.e. it fails if ANY event falls through to that
wildcard walk. That assertion was vacuous until I fixed the fixture to produce signed,
committed events, which is the correction recorded above.

## Two operability asks from that lane are NOT in 1739's scope

They ask that (a) the lock holder record identify the holder as optional housekeeping, and
(b) an operator be told that killing it is safe. Both are fair — this kill needed `lsof`/`ps`
to identify a holder that `run_sweep`'s own docstring already guarantees is safe to interrupt.
Neither is trivial: the ownership stamp is the shared v2 format with documented forward-compat
constraints. Filing separately rather than expanding a change that is at LLM-Review +1 with
Verified pending.

Expected until 1739 merges: the killed sweep will be retriggered by the next close on any
worktree, under OLD code. Not chasing it.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The store-wide compaction sweep stalls every writer in the fleet for minutes at a time. Live
operator profiling: "the compaction spawns a fresh git log --full-history child every few
seconds (7268 → 7496 …), each at ~100% CPU, holding the global write lock throughout."

Cause, confirmed in code. `_compact_locked` builds the SNAPSHOT authorship ledger via
`_build_authorship_ledger` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:72`), which calls
`authorship.build_ticket_position_commit_map` (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:294`) — one
`git log --full-history` walk PER TICKET, executed INSIDE the store write lock.

This is bug 7084 recurring one scale up. 7084 found the same walk running per SIGNED EVENT
(6.78s/event on a 71,041-commit branch; 47.5s of a 48.1s compact-on-close whose real mutation
is ~0.4s) and batched it to per-TICKET (0.53s for an 18-file ticket, 3.83s for a 159-file one).
That was right for compact-on-close, which folds one ticket. Story
`gaudy-gangrenous-basilisk` made `compact-all` the store's standing sweep, so the same call now
runs once per ticket across thousands of tickets — per-ticket became the new per-event.

Two secondary defects in the same path:
- `_commit_backfill` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:275`) stages with an unscoped
  `git add -A`, so a concurrent writer's in-flight event files can be committed under the
  compactor's "chore: backfill SNAPSHOT files" message.
- The sweep never re-yields mid-run: `compact_trigger.run_sweep` probes `write_lock_is_busy`
  once before starting, and the per-ticket loop that follows — in `compact_all_cli`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:386`) — never probes again, so writers arriving after the
  sweep starts wait for the whole run.

## Approach
Batch the read-only prep with no lock held, then take short lock windows for mutations only.

**1. Hoist the history walk out of the lock.** `git log` is read-only and never needed the
write lock. Resolve the ledger's introducing-commit data before acquiring; then lock, re-check
the ticket's event set is unchanged, write the SNAPSHOT, retire sources, commit, release. Same
verify-outside-lock discipline as the original P0 fix, one layer down. A changed event set means
the prepared fold is stale — abort that ticket cleanly and let the next pass take it.

**2. Amortize the walk with the primitive that already exists.** Do not write a new batcher:
`authorship.build_position_commit_map` (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:466`) already maps every
event POSITION to the oldest commit that added its file in a SINGLE pass, walking history once
and falling back to the per-entry resolver (fail-closed) for anything it misses. Build it ONCE
per sweep and query it per ticket, replacing N directory-scoped walks with one.

The POSITION-keyed builder is the load-bearing detail. Its path-keyed sibling
`build_introducing_commit_map` (`:388`) looks equally applicable and is the wrong one:
`_build_authorship_ledger` looks up `position_commits.get(position_str)`
(`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:127`), so a path-keyed map would miss every lookup, and
every event would fall through to the per-event `resolve_event_commit` — silently
re-introducing the exact per-event walks this ticket exists to remove, with correct output and
no error to notice. The ledger-parity acceptance criterion below is not enough to catch that
on its own, which is why one criterion asserts the WALK COUNT directly.

With the walk gone from the critical section, the per-ticket lock window is the SNAPSHOT write,
the renames and the commit — the ~0.4s that 7084's own measurement attributed to real mutation.
That subsumes chunking: the hold is already bounded by one ticket's mutation.

**3. Scope the staging and re-yield.** Commit only the paths the sweep folded rather than
`git add -A`, and re-probe `write_lock_is_busy` between tickets so a sweep that began on a quiet
store stands aside when writers arrive.

The new map parameter on `_build_authorship_ledger` is OPTIONAL (keyword, default `None`), and
that is a compatibility requirement rather than a style choice. The function has a second
consumer, `compact_rebuild.py:160` (the fsck SNAPSHOT-rebuild path), plus six existing test call
sites that pass `(paths, None)` or `(paths, repo_root=...)` positionally. The rebuild path folds
ONE ticket, so a per-ticket walk is already the right cost there and it stays UNCHANGED — it
simply omits the new argument and keeps building its own map. Only the sweep supplies one.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py` — accept an OPTIONAL prebuilt commit map (default
  `None`, preserving `compact_rebuild.py:160` and the existing test call sites unchanged);
  hoist ledger prep out of the locked section; re-check the event set under the lock.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — build the map once per sweep and thread it through; scope
  `_commit_backfill`'s staging to the folded paths; re-probe `write_lock_is_busy` between
  tickets in `compact_all_cli`'s loop, which is where the per-ticket iteration actually lives.
- `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py` — new tests.

## Testing
- A sweep over N tickets performs ONE history walk, not N — asserted by counting calls to the
  map builder, not by timing.
- No `git log` child is spawned while the store write lock is held — asserted structurally, by
  instrumenting the lock and the walk, never by a duration.
- An event appended to a ticket between prep and the locked re-check aborts that ticket's fold
  cleanly, writes no SNAPSHOT, and leaves its events live for the next pass.
- The ledger produced with a prebuilt map is byte-identical to the one produced by the
  per-ticket walk, over a store containing signed, unsigned and forged-signature events.
- The rebuild path is untouched: `compact_rebuild`'s ledger is unchanged when it omits the new
  argument, so the fsck rebuild keeps its current behaviour.
- `_commit_backfill` commits only the folded paths: a concurrent writer's uncommitted event file
  present during the sweep is NOT included in the compaction commit.
- A sweep re-yields: with the store lock taken after the sweep starts, `compact_all_cli` stops
  folding further tickets and leaves the rest live.
- The prebuilt map is actually CONSULTED: a sweep with the map supplied performs no per-ticket
  walk, proving the key shapes match rather than silently falling back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A store-wide sweep performs exactly one history walk regardless of ticket count — a test
      counts BOTH the per-sweep builder and the per-ticket/per-event resolvers, so a key-shape
      mismatch that silently falls back to per-event walks fails the test rather than passing
      on identical output.
- [ ] No history walk runs inside the store write lock — a test instruments both and asserts
      no walk observes the lock held.
- [ ] A ticket whose events change between prep and the locked re-check is skipped cleanly:
      no SNAPSHOT, no retired sources, events still live, exit 0.
- [ ] The authorship ledger is unchanged by the optimisation — a test compares ledgers built
      with and without the prebuilt map on signed, unsigned and forged-signature events.
- [ ] The map argument is optional and the fsck rebuild path is unaffected — a test calls
      `_build_authorship_ledger` without it (as `compact_rebuild.py:160` does) and asserts the
      same ledger as before.
- [ ] The compaction commit contains only folded paths — a test asserts a concurrent writer's
      uncommitted event file is not swept into it.
- [ ] A sweep stands aside mid-run when a writer takes the lock, leaving remaining tickets
      unfolded — and the full local gate set plus CI's pytest tiers pass.

file_impact.reason: accept a prebuilt position-keyed commit map, hoist ledger prep out of the locked section, re-check the event set under the lock
build the position map once per sweep and thread it through; scope _commit_backfill staging to folded paths; re-probe the store lock between tickets in the sweep loop
tests for one-walk-per-sweep including no per-event fallback, no walk under the lock, TOCTOU skip, ledger parity, scoped staging and mid-run re-yield
